function.description: Get the President and Vice President of United States for a specified year. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

We have a tool get_president_and_vp(year, position). We can call it twice for each query? Actually we need four calls: (1980, 'president'), (2016, 'president'), (1975, 'vice president'), (2011, 'vice president').

We should use the function. We'll produce separate calls? The instructions say "When you want to use a tool, respond with a JSON object containing the name of the function to call and arguments." So we need to output a single function call? But we might need multiple calls. Usually we can chain calls: first call get_president_and_vp for 1980 president, then next for 2016 president, etc. But maybe we can combine? The function signature only accepts one year and position. So we need separate calls.

Thus we will do four calls sequentially. We'll start with 1980 president. Then after receiving result, we can proceed to next. But the system expects us to output a function call JSON. After we get response, we can continue. Let's do first call.
